$comment: Sealed golden bundles. See README.md before touching anything in this directory.

goldens.why: A real exporter's output across 8 module databases, carrying the shapes a minimal bundle never exercises: embedded children, numbering watermarks, the resolved-settings sidecar, per-DB snapshot consistency, pseudonymized values.
goldens.provenance: backends examples/acme-mini (the Phase-4 committed fixture, produced by the real exporter)
goldens.roleReason: Real exporter output, so it is genuine evidence that the shipping exporter and the shipping validator agree. Kept pre-GA as a cheap smoke test.

$roles.importer: Tier 1 (verify + digest + resourceVersion + FIELD compatibility against the current entity manifest) and tier 2 (restored into a real stack, run locally).

$corpusStatus: PRE-GA. The 36-month window counts bundles ISSUED TO CUSTOMERS, and there are none yet — so this corpus guards nothing today and is deliberately minimal. At first production release, seal ONE bundle from the production exporter as era zero; that is when the window starts and when tier 2 is worth re-enabling in CI. Two pre-production fixtures (1.0-minimal, 1.0-adapter) were retired from the corpus on 2026-08-15 for exactly this reason — they were hand-written/synthetic rather than exporter output, which is how 1.0-minimal came to carry ten columns that have never existed. Both still live as validator examples under packages/ember-validator/examples/.
